context.analysis:
## Overview
An Amazon-style global e-commerce platform designed to sell physical and electronic books with integrated reviews, recommendations, and multi-currency support. It provides high availability and low latency for millions of users across multiple AWS regions.

## Key Elements
* **Book Buyer:** Primary customer interacting via web/mobile frontends.
* **Store Administrator & Author/Publisher Partner:** Administrative users managing catalogues, permissions, and analytics.
* **AWS CloudFront & WAF:** Edge caching and security boundary.
* **API Gateway & Microservices:** Core containers handling catalogue, cart, checkout, reviews, and recommendations.
* **External Systems:** Third-Party Payment Gateways and Shipping APIs.

## Relationships
* **Book Buyer to CloudFront/WAF:** HTTPS (TLS 1.3) for catalogue browsing, checkout, and reviews.
* **Microservices to Payment Gateway:** HTTPS (TLS 1.2+) with client-side tokenization.
* **Microservices to Shipping APIs:** Asynchronous messaging via Amazon SQS and HTTPS.
* **Services to Databases:** Encrypted TCP connections to regional read replicas and KMS.

## Technology Stack
* **Cloud Infrastructure:** AWS (`us-east-1`, `eu-west-1`, `ap-southeast-1`) utilizing Route 53 latency-based routing for multi-region scale.
* **Security & Auth:** AWS WAF, KMS, OAuth 2.0 / OIDC, and TLS 1.3 for OWASP Top-10 and GDPR/CCPA compliance.
* **Resilience & Messaging:** Amazon SQS and circuit breakers for decoupling third-party shipping APIs.
* **Performance:** Amazon CloudFront for edge caching static assets to achieve sub-2s load times.

## Rationale
The distributed AWS multi-region architecture guarantees 99.95% uptime and sub-second performance for 1M MAU. Asynchronous queuing and strict data encryption ensure regulatory compliance and operational resilience during third-party outages.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
[A global multi-region e-commerce platform for purchasing physical and electronic books, providing personalized recommendations, reviews, and secure multi-currency checkout.]

## Key Elements
• Book Buyer, Store Administrator, Author/Publisher Partner (Actors)
• AWS CloudFront, AWS WAF, AWS App Mesh (Edge & Networking)
• Amazon ECS/EKS, AWS Lambda@Edge (Compute Containers)
• Catalog & Search, Personalization Engine, Checkout/Payment, Localization/Currency, Notification Containers (Core Containers)
• Third-Party Payment Gateways, Third-Party Shipping APIs (External Systems)

## Relationships
• Book Buyer to AWS CloudFront via HTTPS (TLS 1.3)
• Containers inter-communication via mTLS over AWS App Mesh
• Notification Container to AWS SQS/SNS via encrypted transport (TLS)
• Checkout Container to Third-Party Payment Gateways via secure REST APIs

## Technology Stack
• AWS ECS/EKS: Container orchestration for stateless microservices ensuring scalability (1M MAU)
• AWS App Mesh: Service mesh providing mTLS and traffic isolation
• OpenTelemetry & AWS X-Ray: Distributed tracing and observability sidecars
• AWS Secrets Manager: Secure credential injection via IAM task roles
• AWS KMS: Data-at-rest encryption (AES-256) for PII and payment tokens
• AWS SQS/SNS: Decoupled asynchronous messaging with dead-letter queues

## Rationale
[Stateless container design combined with regional AWS deployments ensures 99.95% uptime and sub-2-second page loads globally. Strict mTLS trust boundaries, IAM least privilege, and AES-256 encryption satisfy stringent GDPR, CCPA, and OWASP security requirements.]

AWS CloudFront & WAF.analysis:
## Overview
Global e-commerce platform for purchasing physical and electronic books with recommendations and reviews. Serves 1 million monthly active users globally with multi-currency support and strict regulatory compliance.

## Key Elements
- Book Buyer, Store Administrator, Author/Publisher Partner (Users)
- AWS CloudFront & WAF (Edge Caching, CDN, and Security)
- Catalog & Search, Personalization Engine, Checkout/Payment, Localization/Currency, Notification Containers (Amazon ECS/EKS)
- Third-Party Payment Gateways and Shipping APIs (External Systems)

## Relationships
- Book Buyer & Partners -> AWS CloudFront & WAF: Accesses platform securely [HTTPS (TLS 1.3)]
- AWS CloudFront & WAF -> Catalog & Search, Personalization, Checkout, Localization: Routes requests [HTTPS / mTLS over AWS App Mesh]
- AWS CloudFront & WAF -> Amazon S3: Origin failover and static asset retrieval [AWS IAM Origin Access Control]

## Technology Stack
- AWS CloudFront & WAF: Global CDN and edge security with AWS WAF Bot Control and Shield Advanced for DDoS mitigation.
- Amazon ECS/EKS: Container orchestration for core microservices across multi-regions (`us-east-1`, `eu-west-1`, `ap-southeast-1`).
- Terraform/CDK: Infrastructure-as-Code for consistent multi-region deployments and automated provisioning.
- AWS Certificate Manager (ACM): TLS 1.3 termination at edge with strict mTLS for backend communication.

## Rationale
Multi-region AWS deployment with edge caching guarantees sub-2-second page loads on 3G networks globally. Comprehensive edge security controls and strict IAM policies fulfill GDPR/CCPA compliance and OWASP Top-10 requirements while maintaining 99.95% uptime.

Catalog & Search.analysis:
## Overview
An AWS-hosted online bookstore e-commerce platform supporting 1M MAU with global catalog browsing, search, and secure multi-currency transactions. The architecture prioritizes sub-2-second page loads and strict GDPR/CCPA compliance across three global regions.

## Key Elements
- **Users**: Book Buyer, Store Administrator, Author/Publisher Partner
- **External Systems**: Third-Party Payment Gateways, Shipping APIs, AWS CloudFront & WAF
- **Containers**: Catalog & Search (Amazon ECS/EKS), Personalization Engine (AWS Lambda@Edge), Checkout/Payment, Localization/Currency, Notification Container
- **Data & Infrastructure**: OpenSearch on AWS, AWS SQS/SNS, Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose, Amazon S3 & Athena, AWS App Mesh

## Relationships
- AWS CloudFront & WAF -> Catalog & Search: Routes requests via HTTPS / mTLS over AWS App Mesh
- Catalog & Search -> OpenSearch on AWS: Executes catalog and keyword queries via private VPC networking
- Catalog & Search -> Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose: Streams asynchronous search telemetry via FluentBit

## Technology Stack
- **Compute & Orchestration**: Amazon ECS/EKS with HPA for container scaling supporting 1M MAU
- **Search & Caching**: OpenSearch on AWS with cross-cluster replication; AWS CloudFront for regional edge caching
- **Networking & Security**: AWS WAF for input sanitization, AWS App Mesh for mTLS, AWS KMS for encryption at rest
- **Analytics & Telemetry**: FluentBit, Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose, Amazon S3, and Amazon Athena for asynchronous PII-masked search analytics

## Rationale
Decoupling search infrastructure via OpenSearch and asynchronous telemetry via Kinesis ensures sub-2-second latency under high loads. Private VPC isolation, mTLS, and automated PII masking satisfy strict security, OWASP, and GDPR/CCPA compliance requirements.

Personalization Engine.analysis:
## Overview
[A secure, scalable microservice-based Personalization Engine that delivers real-time book recommendations while enforcing strict GDPR/CCPA compliance across global AWS regions.]

## Key Elements
* Book Buyer (Primary Persona)
* AWS CloudFront & WAF (Edge Security & Content Delivery)
* AWS Lambda@Edge & Amazon ECS/EKS (Compute Containers)
* Amazon ElastiCache / Redis (Edge Caching & User Vectors)
* Amazon Kinesis / SQS (Asynchronous Ingestion Pipeline)
* AWS App Mesh (Service Mesh for Internal Communication)
* Amazon CloudWatch & AWS X-Ray (Observability & Monitoring)

## Relationships
* AWS CloudFront & WAF -> Personalization Engine: Routes recommendation requests via HTTPS / mTLS over AWS App Mesh
* Book Buyer -> AWS CloudFront: Initiates browsing and recommendation requests
* Lambda@Edge -> Amazon ElastiCache: Queries localized user vectors and cached trending best-sellers
* ECS/EKS Services -> Amazon Kinesis: Streams pseudonymized user interactions asynchronously
* Personalization Engine -> AWS CloudWatch: Publishes telemetry, KPI dashboards, and system metrics

## Technology Stack
* AWS Lambda@Edge: Enables low-latency localized inference at the edge
* Amazon ECS/EKS: Orchestrates containerized recommendation and inference workloads
* Amazon ElastiCache (Redis): Provides high-performance, low-latency in-memory caching for user profiles and trending fallbacks
* Amazon Kinesis / SQS: Decouples interaction tracking to handle high-frequency write spikes asynchronously
* AWS App Mesh & mTLS: Enforces zero-trust internal service-to-service communication
* AES-256 Encryption & Cryptographic Erasure: Secures data at rest and fulfills GDPR "Right to be Forgotten" mandates

## Rationale
[Decoupling ingestion via Kinesis and deploying multi-region caching with Lambda@Edge ensures sub-second responses and 99.95% uptime under high global traffic. Cryptographic erasure and consent-aware fallbacks achieve strict GDPR/CCPA compliance without sacrificing recommendation performance or business conversion rates.]

Checkout/Payment.analysis:
## Overview
The Checkout/Payment system is a secure e-commerce component designed to process multi-currency transactions, manage carts, and integrate with fulfillment services. It guarantees PCI-DSS compliance, GDPR/CCPA data minimization, and 99.95% availability for Book Buyers.

## Key Elements
*   **Book Buyer**: Primary user initiating checkout and managing shopping carts.
*   **AWS CloudFront & WAF**: Edge security layer enforcing rate-limiting and DDoS protection.
*   **Checkout/Payment Container**: Amazon ECS/EKS container managing cart sessions, payment orchestration, and idempotency.
*   **Third-Party Payment Gateways**: External systems processing credit cards and express payments (Apple Pay, Google Pay, PayPal) via client-side tokenization.
*   **Third-Party Shipping APIs**: External providers handling regional shipping and fulfillment calculations.
*   **AWS SQS & DLQ**: Messaging infrastructure managing asynchronous webhooks and automated alerting.

## Relationships
*   Book Buyer -> AWS CloudFront & WAF: Submits secure checkout requests [HTTPS / TLS 1.3]
*   AWS CloudFront & WAF -> Checkout/Payment Container: Routes filtered traffic [HTTPS / mTLS over AWS App Mesh]
*   Checkout/Payment Container -> Third-Party Payment Gateways: Tokenizes data and authorizes transactions [Secure REST APIs via mTLS]
*   Checkout/Payment Container -> Third-Party Shipping APIs: Retrieves rates and dispatches orders [HTTPS]
*   Third-Party Payment Gateways -> Checkout/Payment Container: Sends asynchronous transaction webhooks [HTTPS with HMAC Verification]

## Technology Stack
*   **Amazon ECS/EKS**: Container orchestration platform hosting the checkout services.
*   **KEDA (Kubernetes Event-driven Autoscaling)**: Auto-scales pods based on SQS queue depth for flash sales.
*   **AWS Secrets Manager**: Securely manages outbound API keys and mTLS certificates.
*   **AWS X-Ray**: Distributed tracing tool for monitoring latency bottlenecks and preventing cart abandonment.
*   **AWS WAF**: Edge security filtering malicious traffic and preventing card-testing attacks.

## Rationale
This architecture uses client-side tokenization and mTLS to strictly minimize the PCI-DSS audit boundary while protecting sensitive financial data. KEDA auto-scaling, active-active database replication, and circuit breakers ensure the high availability, scalability, and resilience required for global e-commerce.

Localization/Currency.analysis:
## Overview
The Localization/Currency component provides multi-currency (USD, EUR, GBP) and localized content support for the global e-commerce platform. It ensures low-latency currency conversion, automated geo-detection, and secure user-explicit preference overrides.

## Key Elements
- **Book Buyer**: End-user interacting with the store and currency selectors.
- **AWS CloudFront & WAF**: Edge service handling Geo-IP resolution via viewer headers and routing.
- **AWS Lambda@Edge**: Edge compute for initial request localization and header processing.
- **Localization/Currency Container (Amazon ECS/EKS)**: Core backend component managing currency logic and overrides.
- **AWS ElastiCache (Redis)**: Distributed cache storing synced exchange rates globally via Global Datastores.
- **AWS EventBridge & Lambda**: Background worker pipeline for periodic exchange rate synchronization.
- **AWS Secrets Manager**: Secure storage for third-party exchange rate API keys.

## Relationships
- **AWS CloudFront & WAF -> Localization/Currency**: Routes requests via HTTPS / mTLS over AWS App Mesh.
- **AWS EventBridge & Lambda -> External Exchange Rate APIs**: Fetches market rates periodically via HTTPS.
- **Localization/Currency -> AWS ElastiCache**: Reads cached exchange rates via Redis protocol.
- **Localization/Currency -> AWS Secrets Manager**: Retrieves API credentials securely using AWS SDK.

## Technology Stack
- **Amazon ECS/EKS**: Container orchestration for scalable microservice deployment.
- **AWS ElastiCache Redis**: Distributed caching for low-latency exchange rate retrieval (<2s page load).
- **AWS App Mesh & mTLS**: Secures service-to-service communication within the mesh.
- **AWS Secrets Manager**: Isolates sensitive API credentials with automatic rotation.

## Rationale
Decoupling exchange rate fetching via asynchronous background sync and regional ElastiCache replication prevents single points of failure, protecting the 99.95% uptime SLA and <2s page load requirement. Offloading geo-detection to the edge combined with secure session-bound overrides ensures regulatory compliance (GDPR/CCPA) and an optimized global user experience.

Notification Container.analysis:
## Overview
[The Notification Container is a cloud-native microservice responsible for dispatching asynchronous order updates, shipping notifications, and alerts while ensuring strict GDPR/CCPA compliance and high availability across global AWS regions.]

## Key Elements
- Book Buyer & Author/Publisher Partner
- Notification Container (Amazon ECS/EKS)
- AWS SQS / SNS (Regional Message Queues & Topics)
- Amazon ElastiCache / Redis (Consent & Preference Cache)
- AWS KMS & AWS Secrets Manager
- Third-Party Shipping & Notification APIs

## Relationships
- Checkout/Payment Container -> Notification Container: Publishes cryptographically signed messages [AWS SNS/SQS]
- Notification Container -> Amazon ElastiCache/Redis: Validates real-time user consent [TCP/In-Memory]
- Notification Container -> Third-Party Shipping APIs: Dispatches fulfillment updates and alerts [HTTPS / TLS 1.3]
- Notification Container -> AWS Secrets Manager: Fetches dynamic provider API credentials [AWS API]

## Technology Stack
- Amazon ECS/EKS: Orchestrates containerized notification workers with auto-scaling based on SQS queue depth
- AWS SQS/SNS: Manages asynchronous message delivery with Dead Letter Queues (DLQ) for fault tolerance
- Amazon ElastiCache (Redis): Provides low-latency caching for real-time user preference validation
- AWS KMS & AWS Secrets Manager: Secures PII encryption at rest and dynamic credential management
- AWS X-Ray / OpenTelemetry: Enables distributed tracing across event pipelines

## Rationale
[This decoupled architecture ensures 99.95% uptime and high scalability to handle bursty traffic without degrading performance. Robust security controls, including PII encryption, least-privilege IAM, and strict egress filtering, guarantee OWASP and GDPR/CCPA compliance.]
